[context_summary]
Task: Write /app/mystery.c in C that, when compiled with `gcc -static -o reversed mystery.c -lm` and run as `./reversed`, reproduces identical behavior/output (stdout text + image.ppm, P3 800x600) as the compiled AArch64 statically-linked binary /app/mystery. Constraints: mystery.c gzip-compressed <2k; must not invoke ./mystery; must be a fully independent self-contained C program.

Host is AArch64 (`uname -m` = aarch64), so we can compile/run and compare directly against the reference. Reference image /app/image.ppm (md5 40e1aa07264a0e380d662007f17d9a42) matches exactly what ./mystery produces (confirmed by running it in /tmp/run1).

What I know about the binary:
- Symbols: main(0x400600), vector_normalize(0x400d80, takes 3 floats in s0,s1,s2, returns normalized), allocate_image/write_image/free_image, sphere_intersect(0x400e40), plus unused helpers (trace, sky_color, is_in_shadow, plane_intersect).
- Output strings (rodata at 0x456000): "Creating high-resolution image: %dx%d\n", "This will be downsampled with ffmpeg after rendering\n" (53 bytes), "Rendering high-resolution image...\n" (35 bytes), "\rProgress: %.1f%%" (per row, printed as double percent = (float)(r*100.0f/600.0f)), "Rendering complete\n", "Wrote image to %s\n", "Done.\n". Filename "image.ppm".
- write_image: opens "image.ppm" ("w"), fprintf "P3\n%d %d\n255\n", then per pixel prints "%d %d %d\n" with values = fcvtzs(clamp01(float)*255.0f); pixel stored as 3 consecutive floats.
- allocate_image(800,600): array of 600 row pointers, each 800*3 floats.

Sphere_intersect semantics (verified via disassembly; fnmsub test confirmed: fnmsub Vd,Vn,Vm,Va = Vn*Vm - Va):
- input ray (packed 6
[/context_summary]
